summary: Private deployment: intermittent DNS resolution and TLS handshake failures for control-plane egress (customer VPC)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's Redwood Private control-plane is intermittently failing to resolve control-plane FQDNs from inside their VPC, and when DNS does resolve the TLS handshake to our API endpoints times out or drops with an SNI/TLS error. This started after the customer enabled a more restrictive egress firewall policy and a new on-prem DNS forwarder.

Impact:
- Production inference requests fail ~20% of the time across multiple services; observed client errors are DNS resolution failures and TLS handshake timeouts.
- Customer reports model pulls failed during model startup causing 503 spikes and degraded throughput.
- Affects FinEdge Analytics' reporting pipelines and real-time inference for fraud alerts.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (control plane + private agents)
- Customer VPC: AWS eu-west-1, private subnets with NAT Gateway behind a transit VPC and on-prem VPN
- Network controls: enterprise firewall (named "FE-FW-1"), internal DNS forwarder (10.12.0.5) that forwards to corporate resolvers, strict egress ACLs allowing only specific IP ranges and ports 80/443

Steps to reproduce (as performed by support):
1) From a private agent EC2 instance in customer's VPC: curl -v https://control.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/models
2) Observe intermittent "Could not resolve host" or long stalls followed by TLS alert "handshake failure" in openssl s_client -connect control.redwood-inference.example.com:443 -servername control.redwood-inference.example.com
3) Meanwhile from a bastion host in same subnet with unrestricted egress, requests succeed consistently.

Representative logs / commands (redacted):
- curl: "curl: (6) Could not resolve host: control.redwood-inference.example.com"
- openssl: "140735058823424:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1528:SSL alert number 40"
- tcpdump (captured on instance): repeated DNS queries to 10.12.0.5 with no response for ~15s, then occasional forwarded query out to corp-resolver that returns NXDOMAIN for control.redwood-inference.example.com

Initial investigation notes / hypothesis:
- DNS: The customer's internal DNS forwarder sometimes returns NXDOMAIN or drops queries for our control-plane FQDN; observed correlation between NXDOMAIN responses and curl failures. Potentially due to DNS RBAC/filtering or split-horizon rules not including Redwood domains.
- Egress/firewall: Customer's firewall allows outbound 443 but blocks or drops connections when SNI matches unknown domains (inspection device performing TLS interception). The openssl error and packet traces suggest a TLS inspection device may be terminating or resetting flows when SNI doesn't match an allowlist.
- VPC peering / routing: Not primary — routing between subnets appears correct and bastion host in same subnet can reach endpoints. Points to egress/DNS path or proxy.

Immediate customer-facing workaround suggested (applied by customer):
- Configure internal DNS forwarder to allow/forward queries for *.redwood-inference.example.com to public resolvers OR add a static A record for control.redwood-inference.example.com pointing to our documented control-plane IP set.
- Temporarily bypass corporate TLS inspection for Redwood endpoints by adding exception in the firewall for SNI *.redwood-inference.example.com (customer has applied and saw immediate reduction in TLS failures).

Next steps (Support/SRE owner):
1) Request customer's firewall and DNS team to capture full packet traces for failed flows and DNS logs for timestamps 2026-03-09T08:00Z - 2026-03-09T10:30Z (customer provided initial captures).
2) We will provide a list of canonical outbound FQDNs and current IP prefix list for control-plane endpoints and model storage endpoints (deliverable: control-plane-fqdns-2026-03-14.txt).
3) Verify whether TLS interception causes certificate mismatch by having customer capture TLS cert presented during failures (or run s_client -showcerts) and share.
4) If corporate DNS continues to return NXDOMAIN, advise adding conditional forwarder or static records.
5) Explore long-term options: support VPC endpoints / private-link for control plane or explicit VPC peering to avoid corporate egress inspection for mission-critical traffic.

Notes: customer is on a Private plan with high security requirements and requires written guidance they can give to their network/security teams. They asked for a timeline to resolution and for an interim SLA workaround to avoid production impact.

2026-03-10 11:45 - FinEdge Network Engineer (customer): Captured tcpdump showing DNS queries to 10.12.0.5 and NXDOMAIN responses for control.redwood-inference.example.com. Will request firewall team to check TLS inspection logs.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Hypothesis: corporate DNS forwarder is applying a blocklist or split-horizon that doesn't resolve our domains. Also possible TLS proxy is breaking SNI. Request customer to bypass TLS inspection for our FQDN as a test.

2026-03-12 14:05 - FinEdge Security (customer): Temporary firewall exception added for SNI *.redwood-inference.example.com. Observed drop in TLS failures from ~20% to ~2% immediately. DNS NXDOMAIN still observed intermittently.

2026-03-13 10:00 - Asha Patel (Support): Uploaded recommended FQDN/IP list and a short runbook for their network team: control-plane FQDNs, model storage endpoints, required ports (443 outbound), and TTL guidance for static records. Asked customer to add conditional forwarder to public resolvers.

2026-03-14 09:30 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Performed review of customer packet captures. Confirmed sequences where firewall returned TCP RST after TLS ClientHello when SNI matched our domain — consistent with TLS interception failure. Filed INT-3310 to evaluate enabling PrivateLink for control plane as an enterprise feature request.
workaround: Customer added temporary SNI exception in firewall and configured static DNS entries for control.redwood-inference.example.com; both reduced errors. Long-term: conditional forwarder or private-link recommended.
follow_up_actions: Provide canonical FQDN/IP list to customer (done)
Engineering to scope PrivateLink/VPC endpoint option (linked INT-3310)
Add 'Private deployment networking checklist' step to onboarding for customers with TLS interception devices
public_notes: For network teams: ensure outbound DNS resolution for *.redwood-inference.example.com and allow TLS passthrough for SNI to avoid interception failures. If egress inspection is mandatory, configure an allowlist for our FQDNs or use our PrivateLink option.
customer_communication_status: Customer notified of interim workaround and ETA for PrivateLink scoping; awaiting confirmation from their network team for DNS conditional forwarder change.
